access.title: API Accounts
access.snippet:
APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/quick-start) that let you manage store data, authenticate customers, make client-side queries for product information, and more. API accounts are used to authenticate requests to our APIs.
There are two different API account types that can be created in the control panel: [store-level API accounts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) that correspond to a single store, and [account-level API accounts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#account-level-api-accounts) that function in all stores within your BigCommerce account.

### Requirements
- Only the [store owner](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/Store-Owner) can create account-level API accounts.
- To view, create, and manage store-level API accounts, you must be granted [high-risk user permissions](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/User-Permissions) by the store owner.
- To view webhooks, you must be granted the **Read Webhooks**[user permission](/articles/en_US/Knowledge/User-Permissions).

- **Subscriptions** — View or cancel [subscriptions](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/storefront/subscriptions/create-subscription) to your store's marketing and abandoned cart emails.
- **Checkouts** — View or create [storefront checkouts](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/storefront/checkouts).
- **Charges** — Create or delete charges via the [Payments API](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/payments).
- **Account** — View account information for Account level [GraphQL](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/storefront/guides/graphql-storefront-api/overview).
- **Account Stores** — View information for stores belonging to the account for Account level GraphQL.

Any apps intended for sale on the BigCommerce App Marketplace must use OAuth. OAuth is compatible with all current and planned BigCommerce APIs, including v2 Webhooks and our v3 API. For more information, see our documentation on [Authentication](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts) in our Developer Docs.

access.title: BigCommerce Docs
access.snippet:
BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials. This section describes the difference between the three, how to obtain and revoke account credentials, and the use cases for each. It also contains a reference for available OAuth scopes and provides a compelling list of reasons to migrate from legacy API tokens to OAuth credentials.
Every parent set of API credentials that you request for your store is its own **API account**. At its simplest, an API account consists of the following:
- The `client_id` uniquely identifies the app or user, or the *client*, making a request.
- The `client_secret` is a cryptographically secure value known only to the client and BigCommerce.
Every active API account has at least one `access_token`. [Store-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) include a static access token that does not change. [App-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#app-level-api-accounts) expect each application to generate a unique access token for every store that installs the app. [Account-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#account-level-api-accounts) include a single access token that belongs to the parent account of the store that the user is signed in to at the time of creation.

access.title: B2B Edition Overview
access.snippet:
Before you can start building a custom B2B solution, you’ll need a developer sandbox that can access our APIs. Use these steps to obtain the necessary tools and proceed with your development workflow.
### Create a Sandbox Store
To request a non-transactional sandbox store for development, fill out the form located in the “Create A Sandbox Store” step of the [BigCommerce API Overview](/developer/api-reference/about-our-apis). The developer sandbox is free of charge.
To request B2B Edition provisioning on your store, install the [B2B Edition app](https://www.bigcommerce.com/apps/b2b-edition/) from the marketplace and then [contact our support team](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/#contact) to start the process. If you are a [BigCommerce Partner](https://www.bigcommerce.com/partners/become-a-partner/), reach out to your partner manager to request B2B Edition.

You can [create an API account](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/B2B-Edition-Settings) from **Settings** > **API Accounts** in your B2B Edition control panel to authenticate requests to the REST Management API. You can also generate management and storefront tokens via API requests.

access.title: Beginning App Development
access.snippet:
Before you register and install a draft app, you need the following:
1. A BigCommerce store to test app installation. You can use any store you own. Partners can also create a [sandbox store](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/sandboxes).
2. A [Developer Portal](https://build.bigcommerce.com/) account (required to register apps).
3. A [BigCommerce partnership](https://www.bigcommerce.com/partners/) (required to publish apps to the App Marketplace). To apply, see [Becoming a partner](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/integrations/becoming-a-partner).

mcp.title: docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview
mcp.snippet:
> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
# MCP Server Overview
> Connect AI agents to BigCommerce storefronts using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Search products, manage carts, and hand off to checkout through natural language.
An MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol so AI agents — like Claude, Cursor, and others — can discover and call tools over a standard protocol. In practice, an MCP server exposes a set of functions that agents can call to accomplish real-world tasks.
The BigCommerce MCP server lets AI agents interact with a BigCommerce storefront using purpose-built commerce tools. Agents can search products, manage a shopping cart, and hand off to checkout — all through natural language.
## Available tool sets
| Tool set                                                      | Authentication                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| [B2C Storefront](/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/b2c) | Guest and logged-in customer shopping flows                 |
| [B2B Storefront](/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/b2b) | Authenticated Buyer Portal user, gated per buyer permission |
Both tool sets are served from the same MCP endpoint, and B2C tools aren't exclusive to B2C stores: the catalog, cart, and checkout tools stay available to every session on a B2B-enabled store too, including guests — that's how a B2B store serves unauthenticated shoppers. The B2B tool set adds the Buyer Portal–specific tools (shopping lists, quotes) on top of that, gated per store by B2B Edition and per tool by the authenticated buyer's permissions. Logged-in B2C shoppers and B2B buyers both authenticate the same way — see [Connecting with session sync](#connecting-with-session-sync-stencil-storefronts) below.

In the BigCommerce control panel, go to **Settings**. Under **API and MCP**, select **MCP**.

#### Claude Desktop
In **Claude Desktop**, go to **Settings → Developer → Edit Config** and add the following:
**`claude_desktop_config.json`**
```json title="claude_desktop_config.json" showLineNumbers={false}
{
"mcpServers": {
"bigcommerce": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["mcp-remote", "<YOUR_MCP_SERVER_URL>"]
}
}
}
```

mcp.title: Docs MCP Server
mcp.snippet:
Connect the BigCommerce developer docs to your AI agent so it can answer questions grounded in our documentation.
The docs site exposes a **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server** that AI tools can search and reference. Once connected, your AI tool can answer questions like *“How does the BigCommerce checkout API work?”* by pulling directly from the docs.
Docs search only
This server lets your AI tool search and reference the BigCommerce documentation. It can’t read or change your store, orders, catalog, or account settings. If you’re looking for an MCP server that interacts with your storefront, see the [BigCommerce MCP Server](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview). For everything else, use the [REST and GraphQL APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference).

# BigCommerce MCP Server
A comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for BigCommerce REST API integration. This server provides AI assistants with the ability to interact with BigCommerce stores through three powerful tools:
- 🛍️ **Products Management**: Get all products with advanced filtering
- 👥 **Customer Management**: Retrieve and filter customers with comprehensive search options
- 📦 **Order Management**: Access orders with customer-product relationship capabilities
## ✨ Features
- ✅ MCP-compatible server with built-in tool discovery
- ✅ Enhanced filtering capabilities on all endpoints
- ✅ Customer-product association through order history
- ✅ Comprehensive error handling and validation
- ✅ Docker support for production deployment
- ✅ Compatible with Claude Desktop, Cline, and other MCP clients

**1. Clone and install dependencies**
```
git clone https://github.com/isaacgounton/bigcommerce-api-mcp.git
cd bigcommerce-api-mcp
npm install
```
**2. Configure your BigCommerce credentials**
Create a `.env` file in the project root:
```
BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH=your_store_hash_here
BIGCOMMERCE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```
**How to get your BigCommerce credentials:**
1. Go to your BigCommerce admin panel
2. Navigate to **Advanced Settings** > **API Accounts**
3. Create a new API account with the following scopes:
- **Products**: Read-only or Modify
- **Orders**: Read-only or Modify
- **Customers**: Read-only or Modify
4. Copy the **Store Hash** and **Access Token** to your `.env` file

- Retrieve products from your BigCommerce store

mcp.title: docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/beta/store-management-mcp
mcp.snippet:
> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
# Store Management MCP
> Connect an MCP-compatible AI agent to your BigCommerce store to manage catalog, pricing, inventory, and promotions, to look up and refund orders, and to read store details.
Store Management MCP lets an AI agent — Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or any other Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible client — work directly with your BigCommerce store's catalog, pricing, inventory, orders, promotions, and store profile. This guide covers how an administrator turns on access, how to connect a client, and how to use the tools available in the closed beta.

### Server address
Each store has its own MCP address:
```text showLineNumbers={false}
https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/mcp
```
Point your MCP client at the address for the store you want to connect. Because the address identifies the store, the connection flow has no separate store picker.
### Authentication
Connections use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Your MCP client registers itself automatically, so there's no client ID or client secret to create or manage.
When you connect, your client sends you to the standard BigCommerce login. Your agent never sees or holds your BigCommerce password, session, or any other credential. If your login normally uses two-factor authentication or single sign-on, it works the same way here.
The scopes assigned to your BigCommerce user (see [Grant a user access](#grant-a-user-access-to-connect-an-agent)) determine which tools your agent can see after you sign in. Every tool call is checked against those scopes on the server, on every request — nothing your agent sends is trusted to establish its identity or permissions.

# bigcommerce-mcp-server-by-cdata
CData's Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for BigCommerce
❗ This project builds a local, read-only MCP server. For fully remote MCP access, check out the first managed MCP platform: [CData Connect AI](https://www.cdata.com/ai/). For locally hosted, full read, write, update, delete, and action capabilities and a simplified setup, check out our [CData MCP Server for BigCommerce](https://www.cdata.com/drivers/bigcommerce/download/mcp/).
## Purpose
We created this read-only MCP Server to allow LLMs (like Claude Desktop) to query live data BigCommerce supported by the [CData JDBC Driver for BigCommerce](https://www.cdata.com/drivers/bigcommerce/jdbc/).
CData JDBC Driver connects to BigCommerce by exposing them as relational SQL models.
This server wraps that driver and makes BigCommerce data available through a simple MCP interface, so LLMs can retrieve live information by asking natural language questions — no SQL required.
## Setup Guide
1. Clone the repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/cdatasoftware/bigcommerce-mcp-server-by-cdata.git
cd bigcommerce-mcp-server-by-cdata
```
2. Build the server:
```
mvn clean install
```
This creates the JAR file: CDataMCP-jar-with-dependencies.jar
3. Download and install the CData JDBC Driver for {source}: [https://www.cdata.com/drivers/bigcommerce/download/jdbc](https://www.cdata.com/drivers/bigcommerce/download/jdbc/)
4. License the CData JDBC Driver:
- Navigate to the `lib` folder in the installation directory, typically:
- (Windows) `C:\Program Files\CData\CData JDBC Driver for BigCommerce\`
- (Mac/Linux) `/Applications/CData JDBC Driver for BigCommerce/`
- Run the command `java -jar cdata.jdbc.bigcommerce.jar --license`
- Enter your name, email, and "TRIAL" (or your license key).

Create a `.prp` file for your JDBC connection (e.g. `bigcommerce.prp`) using the following properties and format:
- **Prefix** - a prefix to be used for the tools exposed
- **ServerName** - a name for your server
- **ServerVersion** - a version for your server
- **DriverPath** - the full path to the JAR file for your JDBC driver
- **DriverClass** - the name of the JDBC Driver Class (e.g. cdata.jdbc.bigcommerce.BigCommerceDriver)
- **JdbcUrl** - the JDBC connection string to use with the CData JDBC Driver to connect to your data (copied from above)
- **Tables** - leave blank to access all data, otherwise you can explicitly declare the tables you wish to create access for

# BigCommerce MCP Server
Complete Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for BigCommerce API with **148 production-ready tools** and **24 interactive React apps** covering the entire e-commerce platform.
## 🚀 Features
- ✅ **148 MCP Tools** - Complete coverage of BigCommerce Catalog, Orders, Customers, Marketing, Shipping, and Store Configuration APIs
- ✅ **24 Interactive Apps** - React-based UIs for product management, order fulfillment, customer engagement, analytics, and more
- ✅ **Full TypeScript** - End-to-end type safety with comprehensive BigCommerce type definitions
- ✅ **Dual API Support** - Seamless integration with both v2 (legacy) and v3 (modern) BigCommerce APIs
- ✅ **Production Ready** - Built-in rate limiting, error handling, retry logic, and connection pooling
- ✅ **Zero Config** - Works out of the box with environment variables
---
## 📦 Installation
```
npm install @mcpengine/bigcommerce
```
Or clone and build locally:
```
git clone https://github.com/BusyBee3333/mcpengine.git
cd mcpengine/servers/bigcommerce
npm install
npm run build
```
---
## ⚙️ Configuration
### Environment Variables
Set the following required variables:
```
export BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH="your-store-hash"
export BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN="your-access-token"
```
### Get Your API Credentials
1. Log in to your BigCommerce store admin panel
2. Navigate to **Settings** → **API** → **Store-level API accounts**
3. Click **Create API Account** → **Create V2/V3 API Token**
4. Select OAuth scopes (Products, Orders, Customers, Carts, Marketing, etc.)
5. Copy your **Store Hash** and **Access Token**
6. **Store Hash** format: `abc123def` (found in your store URL: `store-{hash}.mybigcommerce.com`)
### Claude Desktop Configuration
Add to your `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"bigcommerce": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@mcpengine/bigcommerce"],
"env": {
"BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH": "your-store-hash",
"BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your-access-token"
}
}
}
}
```
---
## 🛠️ Usage
### Stdio Transport (Claude Desktop, Cline, etc.)
```
bigcommerce-mcp
```
### Programmatic Usage
```
import { BigCommerceClient } from '@mcpengine/bigcommerce';
const client = new BigCommerceClient({
storeHash: process.env.BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH!,
accessToken: process.env.BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
apiVersion: 'v3', // or 'v2' for legacy endpoints
});
// Fetch products
const products = await client.get('/catalog/products?limit=50');
console.log(products);
```
